div.div: How a request finds a cached answer

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 42px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: Semantic cache is a superset of simple cache, so the gateway tries an exact match first and only embeds the prompt when that misses. Every gate below is a reason a hit you expected did not happen.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 91px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 544px; height: 1px; padding-top: 130px; margin-left: 37px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 536px; height: 1px; padding-top: 185px; margin-left: 35px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Is a cache block set in the config?
div.span: Top level or per target. A target-level block wins over a top-level one.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 536px; height: 1px; padding-top: 259px; margin-left: 35px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: The full request body, the metadata header, and the cache namespace all have to match a stored entry, and that entry has to be inside its max_age. One changed character is a miss.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 536px; height: 1px; padding-top: 351px; margin-left: 35px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Simple mode stops here. Semantic mode carries on.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 536px; height: 1px; padding-top: 421px; margin-left: 35px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Is the request eligible for semantic matching?
div.span: Route is /chat/completions or /completions. Under 8,191 tokens. Four messages or fewer. At least one user message present, since a request carrying only system messages is dropped.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 536px; height: 1px; padding-top: 517px; margin-left: 35px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Embed the user text and search the vector store
div.span: A hit needs cosine similarity above the threshold (0.95 by default) and an exact match on the model and every other body parameter and on the metadata header. The system prompt is ignored, so changing it neither causes nor prevents a hit.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 536px; height: 1px; padding-top: 625px; margin-left: 35px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Call the provider, then store the response as a new entry
div.span: The first request for any prompt always lands here, and so does every request sent with x-portkey-cache-force-refresh: true.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 212px; height: 1px; padding-top: 184px; margin-left: 663px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Also what you get when x-portkey-debug is false, which switches caching off entirely.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 212px; height: 1px; padding-top: 258px; margin-left: 663px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Served from Redis. No provider call, no provider cost, and the latency saving shows on the Analytics cache tab.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 212px; height: 1px; padding-top: 516px; margin-left: 663px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: A differently worded prompt served the stored answer. Logged under its own status so you can tell the two hit types apart.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 212px; height: 1px; padding-top: 624px; margin-left: 663px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Or Cache Refreshed when the force-refresh header was set. For a semantic hit, that header refreshes every matching entry, not just one.

div.div: WHAT A SELF-HOSTED GATEWAY NEEDS FOR SEMANTIC MODE

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 468px; height: 1px; padding-top: 125px; margin-left: 943px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: One of openai, azure-openai, google, or vertex-ai. The gateway calls it on every eligible request that misses the exact-match check.

SEMANTIC_CACHE_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER
SEMANTIC_CACHE_EMBEDDINGS_URL
SEMANTIC_CACHE_EMBEDDING_MODEL
SEMANTIC_CACHE_EMBEDDING_API_KEY
SEMANTIC_CACHE_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS
SEMANTIC_CACHE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD
Azure OpenAI takes a plain API key here. Managed identity and Entra token auth are not supported for this one call.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 468px; height: 1px; padding-top: 387px; margin-left: 943px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Milvus or Pinecone, holding the embeddings the similarity search runs against.

Milvus — name the collection after the embedding model, give it id (Varchar), values (FloatVector at the configured dimension) and metadata (JSON).
Pinecone — omit the collection name, set the address to the index name, and create the index with cosine as its metric.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 468px; height: 1px; padding-top: 615px; margin-left: 943px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: The cached responses themselves live in the gateway's Redis. The vector store holds only the embeddings used to find them, so the two have to be sized and retained together.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 727px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1392px; height: 1px; padding-top: 757px; margin-left: 17px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
• TTL comes from max_age on the cache block: 60 seconds minimum, 90 days maximum, 7 days when you leave it out. An organisation default set under Admin Settings wins whenever a request asks for longer than it, so a per-request value can only ever shorten the lifetime.
• Partitioning is by every request header by default, which is usually why a hit rate looks lower than expected. Send x-portkey-cache-namespace to partition by one string of your choosing instead, per user or per tenant.
• Status appears on every log line as Cache Hit, Cache Semantic Hit, Cache Miss, Cache Refreshed, or Cache Disabled, and the hit rate, latency saving and cost saving roll up on the Analytics cache tab.
